frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a submitted 123 agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all proposed nuclear cooperation agreements formally submitted to Congress under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act. Excludes informal negotiations or agreements not formally transmitted.

coverage_note: 40 major submissions identified across decades; zero successful legislative blocks of a 123 nuclear agreement to date, though related arms sales resolutions have occasionally passed before failing veto overrides.
known_gaps: Classified or minor amendments to existing agreements that did not trigger full formal joint resolutions.
skeleton: Legislative review periods for executive-submitted international agreements since 1970, decomposed into total 123 agreements submitted versus successful veto-proof blocks.
multiplier: Approximately 40 major 123 agreement submissions or renewals over 50 years, yielding 0 successful statutory blocks of a 123 nuclear agreement.
validity_reason: The statutory framework of the Atomic Energy Act Section 123 remains stable, though congressional-executive polarization could shift the baseline over multi-decade horizons.
